title: runtime: emit canary batch composition stats (prefill/decode mix, max seq len)
author: Omar El-Sayed
description:
## Summary
Adds low-overhead batch composition metrics emitted *only* for perf-canary traffic (source=perf-canary). This is intended to help attribute latency/tokens/sec regressions to runtime scheduling/batching behavior changes rather than kernels or hardware.

The metrics are request-scoped and recorded at the batch boundary (i.e., once per executed microbatch), not per token.

## Motivation
During early perf-canary prototyping we saw variance in tokens/sec that correlated with changing prefill/decode mix and a few rare large-seqlen batches. Without explicit batch composition stats, the dashboards can mislead responders into blaming kernels or GPU SKU when the underlying issue is scheduler behavior.

This PR instruments:
- prefill_requests_count / decode_requests_count per executed batch
- max_prefill_seq_len / max_decode_seq_len observed in the batch
- batch_size (total requests in the batch)

All metrics are emitted only when the request has canary tag set (source=perf-canary) to avoid extra overhead and cardinality for customer traffic.

## Metric names (per naming review)
Following Observability guidance (Nadia/Logan) we avoided introducing new label dimensions and kept the naming stable:
- redwood.runtime.canary.batch.prefill_requests (histogram)
- redwood.runtime.canary.batch.decode_requests (histogram)
- redwood.runtime.canary.batch.size (histogram)
- redwood.runtime.canary.batch.max_prefill_seq_len (histogram)
- redwood.runtime.canary.batch.max_decode_seq_len (histogram)

Notes:
- These are histograms to support p50/p95 on composition, but dashboards will generally use p50 and max to detect outliers.
- We intentionally do NOT include per-request prompt length, per-route, or prompt_id labels.
- Existing canary dimensions (model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode) come from the request context and are already in the canary metrics pipeline.

## Implementation
- Hooked into the scheduler’s batch assembly path right before dispatch.
- Aggregates counts and max sequence lengths in a single pass over batch entries.
- Gated on RequestContext::is_perf_canary(). If false, no metric structs are created.

## Tests
- Unit tests validate:
  - gating behavior (no emissions without canary tag)
  - correct counts for mixed prefill+decode batches
  - correct max seq len for prefill/decode
  - stable metric names (string match) to prevent accidental renames

## Risk / overhead
- Additional O(batch_size) scan at dispatch time, but only for canary traffic.
- Uses existing metric exporter; no new high-cardinality labels.

## Follow-ups
- Dashboards: add panels correlating p95 latency with prefill/decode mix (ENG-2847).
- If we find this is still too noisy, we can bucket seq lens into a few fixed ranges at emission time.

---

### Commits
1) runtime: add batch composition aggregation helpers
2) runtime: emit canary batch composition histograms at dispatch
3) runtime: unit tests for gating + max seq len
4) chore(metrics): align names/prefixes with telemetry review feedback

### Changed areas
- serving/runtime/scheduler/*
- serving/runtime/telemetry/*
- serving/runtime/tests/*

### Files changed (high level)
- serving/runtime/scheduler/batch_dispatch.cc
- serving/runtime/scheduler/batch_dispatch.h
- serving/runtime/telemetry/canary_metrics.cc
- serving/runtime/telemetry/canary_metrics.h
- serving/runtime/telemetry/metric_names.h
- serving/runtime/tests/test_canary_batch_metrics.cc

---

## Review conversation (highlights)

**Nadia Rahman (Metrics definitions owner):** Can we avoid adding any new labels? Also, I’d prefer histograms here over gauges so we can look at distribution shifts.

**Omar El-Sayed (author):** Yep—no new labels. These reuse the existing canary label set from context. Switched to histograms and updated tests accordingly.

**Thomas Baird (Cardinality controls):** Please confirm this is hard-gated on canary traffic; we don’t want to accidentally increase runtime metrics volume on customer requests.

**Omar El-Sayed:** Confirmed. The emission function returns early unless RequestContext::is_perf_canary() is true. Added a unit test that asserts the registry sees no samples when tag is missing.

**Logan Wright (Telemetry lead):** Naming: please keep it under `redwood.runtime.canary.batch.*` and avoid abbreviations like `seq`. Also ensure `max_*_seq_len` uses `_len` suffix consistently.

**Omar El-Sayed:** Renamed per suggestion and added a string-match test for metric names to prevent drift.

**Noah Patel (Runtime perf architect):** Where exactly is this hooked? We should not be counting “queued batches”, only “executed batches”.

**Omar El-Sayed:** It’s at dispatch time (right before kernel launch) in batch_dispatch.cc. So it should reflect executed microbatches.

**Sofia Ivanova (Scheduling lead):** Please add a comment clarifying what “prefill vs decode” means in the scheduler data model (first-step vs continuation). People will misread it.

**Omar El-Sayed:** Added a short comment in canary_metrics.h and the test names reflect first-step vs continuation.

---
